text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Miroslav Maxon, deputy of the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), said the governing coalition planned to ask President Michal Kovac not to sign a law postponing banking privatisation.
- Ludovit Cernak of the opposition Democratic Union (DU) said he expected the law to be passed in parliament for the second time after the president returns it at the government's request.

- Some 39 percent of the Slovak population would have voted in favour of Slovakia's membership in NATO if a referendum on the question had been held at the end of January, a public opinion poll showed.

- Slovakia's agricultural sector complains that the state subsidies this year, planned at some 1.8 billion crowns, will not even cover the overall losses for 1996, estimated at some 2.5 billion crowns.

- Slovakia's car sales totalled 4,211 units in January this year, some 1,205 new cars more than in the same month 1995. Czech car maker Skoda led the sales with 1,411 cars, followed by Fiat, selling 586 units.

- An eventual Slovak-Russian free trade agreement will not neccessarily lead to larger mutual trade between the two countries and to a reduction of Slovakia' foreign trade deficit, said Peter Mihok, Chairman of the Slovak Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

PRAVDA - Jan Luptak, leader of the the ultra-left junior coalition member, the Workers Party (ZRS), said ZRS would again vote for the postponement of banking privatisation if Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's HZDS asks president to return the law to parliament.
- The French-Slovak joint-venture GSM operator Globtel said it had about 4,000 customers after the first month of commercial operation.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The overall tax burden in Slovakia was at some 25 percent in 1996, up from 23.9 percent in the previous year.
- The Vienna-based Institute for Comparative Economic Studies sees Slovakia's GDP growth slowing down this year, but still increasing by some five percent.
- Slovakia and Switzerland have signed a double taxation treaty and angreement on cooperation to prevent tax evasions. -- Bratislava Newsrtoom, 42-7-521-8402
